drug_class: Nitrogen scavenger / Urea cycle disorder agent
purpose: Carglumic acid is used to treat a rare inherited condition called N-acetylglutamate synthase (NAGS) deficiency, where the body cannot properly remove ammonia from the blood. It is also used to help lower dangerously high ammonia levels in people with certain other metabolic disorders. Keeping ammonia levels under control is very important because too much ammonia can harm the brain.
how_it_works: Normally, your liver uses a substance called N-acetylglutamate to start a process that converts harmful ammonia into a safe waste product called urea, which you pee out. In NAGS deficiency, your body cannot make enough of this substance. Carglumic acid acts like a substitute for N-acetylglutamate, helping your liver restart this process and clear the excess ammonia from your body.
common_side_effects: Vomiting, nausea, stomach pain, diarrhea, headache, increased sweating, abnormal body temperature (fever or feeling cold), and rash. Some patients may also notice changes in their blood counts, so regular lab checks are important.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have symptoms of high ammonia levels such as confusion, unusual sleepiness, difficulty breathing, or loss of consciousness — this is a medical emergency. This medicine should be used alongside a low-protein diet and other medical management, not alone. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant. Regular blood tests to monitor ammonia levels are very important while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The dose is based on your body weight and is usually taken 2 to 4 times a day with meals. Tablets should be dissolved in a small amount of water (at least 5–10 mL) before swallowing or given through a feeding tube if needed. Your doctor will adjust your dose based on your ammonia blood levels, so follow their instructions closely.
